good: Easy pace. It raises the temperature and rehearses the pull at the same time
Any machine works if there is no rower
bad: Hammering it — this is the raise, not a workout

good: Start small, grow the circle as the shoulder loosens
Backward circles matter more than forward for your sport
bad: Starting with the biggest circle you can make

good: On your side, knees stacked, open the top arm and follow it with your eyes
Get the upper back turning before you ask the shoulder to press
bad: Letting the knees roll apart so the hips do the work

good: Face down, lift the arms a few inches — a Y, then a T
Thumbs up, neck long, no shrugging
Switches on the muscles that hold the shoulder together
bad: Lifting the chest to cheat the arms higher

good: One light set of the first working movement before you load it
Groove the path, feel the shoulder, then go
bad: Going straight to your working weight

good: Hand and knee on the bench, flat back, pull to the hip
Pause at the top, lower it slowly
Pulling leads this session on purpose — it is the half your sport never trains
bad: Twisting the torso to get the dumbbell higher
Dropping it fast and bouncing the next rep

good: Half-kneeling, squeeze the back glute, ribs down
Press straight up beside the ear, not out in front
Kneeling is deliberate — it stops your lower back arching to finish the rep
bad: Leaning back to press the weight up
Pressing through pain. Stop and tell me instead

good: Elbows about 45° from the body, not flared wide
Two sets only, and that is on purpose — your shoulder already presses all week
bad: Adding sets because it feels like the fun one
Letting the elbows flare to ninety degrees

good: Hinge over, light weight, lead with the elbows
Small weight and a real squeeze beats a big weight and a swing
bad: Using the lower back to throw them up
Going so heavy it becomes a row

good: Forearm on your thigh, palm down, very light, slow all the way down
This is the one that keeps tennis elbow away. Two minutes, every week
bad: Going heavy. Light and slow is the whole point
Skipping it because it looks like nothing

good: Pick it up like a deadlift — hips back, flat back, stand up with it
One heavy dumbbell, one side. Walk tall and do not lean away from it
Set it down the same way you picked it up
bad: Bending over and yanking it off the floor
